biography.value:
Organizations: Devotee of Sehanine Moonbow and Corellon Larethian

Allies: Wild Elves, Moonstars. Since he arrived in the vicinity of Daggerford a few years ago (in Elven terms), he has befriended a young human Paladin, Thomas Invictus and has agreed to help him in his recent quests, out of both friendship and curiosity. Jetten's closest friend from his early wanderings is a youngish barbarian Dragonborn named Shea, who he has not seen in 15 years, and considers a brother.

Enemies: Despises followers of Lloth and Gruumsh. Undead of any kind.

Backstory: Over the past 9 years, Jetten has roamed The Sword Coast, The High Forest and the Forlorn Hills acting as an intrepid and (mostly) faithful guide for weary travelers, fat merchants, and pilgrims. In his travels near Daggerford he has befriended a young human Paladin, Thomas Invictus and has agreed to help him in his recent quests, out of both friendship and curiosity. Jetten is from Chondalwood. Jetten left his homelands to Arrabar and thence for the Dalelands and ultimately the Sword Coast. He has made many friends in his journeys, notably a Dragonborn northern barbarian along with a Halfling rogue from Luiren, named Flick, from both he was separated years ago. In his travels around the Realms he always keeps alert for clues to their fate and whereabouts. He still carries a wren-bone whistle with him everywhere, used to imitate birdcall, as a memento of his past adventures with his halfling friend. Other than a thirst for adventure and experience, it is unclear why he originally left his homeland of Chondalwood, perhaps it was due to the frequent conflicts between his elvenkind and their neighbors, perhaps it was a love affair gone bad, or maybe it was just youthful restlessness and a desire to see the wide world; home remains foremost in his heart, however.

Personal Possessions: Moonstone necklace, family heirloom from Chondalwood. Wren-bone whistle as a memento of a treasured friendship.

Other Notes: Jetten places great store in dreams and does not remain in one place for very long.

Personality Traits: Originally from Chondalwood, Jetten left his homelands for the Dalelands and ultimately the Sword Coast, gaining wisdom and many practical experiences. Curious by nature, he has spent his youth patrolling the wilds, always vigilant and prepared. Weather and hardships are comforts to him and he prefers to sleep, if at all, under the stars. He is an intrepid ally and guide.

Ideals: Jetten is devoted to the Goddess Sehanine Moonbow and pays careful attention to her dream visits. He is a loyal ally and unforgiving enemy. He seeks experience and adventure in far lands and ultimately, glory. Although good by nature, he is willing to bend the rules or turn a blind eye to deception or theft in pursuit of a "higher good".

Bonds: Although he is far from home, Chondalwood and his people, and especially his sister, hold a warm space in his heart. He keeps a family heirloom, a Moonstone, close to his heart.

Flaws: Jetten prefers the wilds and does not value many comforts of the city. Newcomers may find him set apart from the rhythm of civilized life; he comes and goes at odd times.

Faith: Sehanine Moonbow

Alignment: Chaotic Good

Physical: Male · Age 110 · 5'8" · 155 lb · Long ash hair, worn tied and clubbed · Pale green eyes · Tan skin

A Wandering Warrior Imbued with Primal Magic

Core Ranger Traits

Primary Ability

Dexterity and Wisdom

Hit Point Die

D10 per Ranger level

Saving Throw Proficiencies

Strength and Dexterity

Skill Proficiencies

Choose 3: Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, or Survival

Weapon Proficiencies

Simple and Martial weapons

Armor Training

Light and Medium armor and Shields

Starting Equipment

Choose A or B: (A) @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbarmStuddedLea]{Studded Leather Armor}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbwepScimitar00]{Scimitar}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbwepShortsword]{Shortsword}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbwepLongbow000]{Longbow}, 20 @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbamoArrows0000]{Arrows}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagQuiver00000]{Quiver}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagDruidicFocu]{Druidic Focus} (@UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbdfcSprigofmis]{sprig of mistletoe}), @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagExplorersPa]{Explorer’s Pack}, and [[/award 7GP]]; or (B) [[/award 150GP]]

Far from bustling cities, amid the trees of trackless forests and across wide plains, Rangers keep their unending watch in the wilderness. Rangers learn to track their quarry as a predator does, moving stealthily through the wilds and hiding themselves in brush and rubble.

Thanks to their connection with nature, Rangers can also cast spells that harness primal powers of the wilderness. A Ranger’s talents and magic are honed with deadly focus to protect the world from the ravages of monsters and tyrants.

Becoming a Ranger …

As a Level 1 Character

  • Gain all the traits in the Core Ranger Traits table.
  • Gain the Ranger’s level 1 features, which are listed in the Ranger Features table.

As a Multiclass Character

  • Gain the following traits from the Core Ranger Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Martial weapons, proficiency in one skill of your choice from the Ranger’s skill list, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields.
  • Gain the Ranger’s level 1 features, which are listed in the Ranger Features table. See the multiclassing rules in chapter 2 to determine your available spell slots.

description.value:
Created by the god Corellon, the first elves could change their forms at will. They lost this ability when Corellon cursed them for plotting with the deity Lolth, who tried and failed to usurp Corellon’s dominion. When Lolth was cast into the Abyss, most elves renounced her and earned Corellon’s forgiveness, but that which Corellon had taken from them was lost forever.

No longer able to shape-shift at will, the elves retreated to the Feywild, where their sorrow was deepened by that plane’s influence. Over time, curiosity led many of them to explore other planes of existence, including worlds in the Material Plane.

Elves have pointed ears and lack facial and body hair. They live for around 750 years, and they don’t sleep but instead enter a trance when they need to rest. In that state, they remain aware of their surroundings while immersing themselves in memories and meditations.

An environment subtly transforms elves after they inhabit it for a millennium or more, and it grants them certain kinds of magic. Drow, high elves, and wood elves are examples of elves who have been transformed thus.

Wood Elves

Wood elves carry the magic of primeval forests within themselves. They are known by many other names, including wild elves, green elves, and forest elves. Grugach are reclusive wood elves of the Greyhawk setting, while the Kagonesti and the Tairnadal are wood elves of the Dragonlance and Eberron settings, respectively.

Elf Traits

Creature Type: Humanoid

Size: Medium (about 5–6 feet tall)

Speed: 30 feet

As an Elf, you have these special traits.

Darkvision. You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

Elven Lineage. You are part of a lineage that grants you supernatural abilities.

When you reach character levels 3 and 5, you learn a higher-level spell, as shown on the table. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the lineage).

Wood Elf Lineage Features

Level 1

Level 3

Level 5

Your Speed increases to 35 feet. You also know the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDruidcraft]{Druidcraft} cantrip.

Keen Senses. You have proficiency in the Insight, Perception, or Survival skill.

Trance. You don’t need to sleep, and magic can’t put you to sleep. You can finish a Long Rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a trancelike meditation, during which you retain consciousness.

You came of age outdoors, far from settled lands. Your home was anywhere you chose to spread your bedroll. There are wonders in the wilderness—strange monsters, pristine forests and streams, overgrown ruins of great halls once trod by giants—and you learned to fend for yourself as you explored them. From time to time, you guided friendly nature priests who instructed you in the fundamentals of channeling the magic of the wild.

Grasping plants sprout from the ground in a 20-foot square within range. For the duration, these plants turn the ground in the area into &Reference[difficultterrain]. They disappear when the spell ends.

Each creature (other than you) in the area when you cast the spell must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have the &Reference[restrained apply=false] condition until the spell ends. A Restrained creature can take an action to make a [[/check ability=str skill=ath dc=@attributes.spell.dc]] check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself from the grasping plants and is no longer Restrained by them.

effects.name: Restrained
effects.description: A Restrained creature can take an action to make a [[/check ability=str skill=ath]] check against your spell save DC. On a success, it frees itself from the grasping plants and is no longer Restrained by them.

Craft: @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagMap00000000]{Map}

A bedroll sleeps one Small or Medium creature. Bundled snug in its quilted layers, a sleeper can pass even a bitterly cold night unharmed — travelers swear no chill has ever bitten through a well-made bedroll.
A Tent sleeps up to two Small or Medium creatures.

A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. When you take the Attack action, you can attack with the Torch, using it as a Simple Melee weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1 Fire damage.
A Waterskin holds up to 4 pints. If you don’t drink sufficient water, you risk &Reference[dehydration].

A @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.equipment.Item.phbagDruidicFocu]{Druidic Focus} takes one of the forms in the Druidic Focuses table and is carved, tied with ribbon, or painted to channel primal magic. A Druid or Ranger can use such an object as a Spellcasting Focus.

You can douse a creature, object, or space with Oil or use it as fuel, as detailed below.

Dousing a Creature or an Object. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing an Oil flask. Target one creature or object within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus) or be covered in oil. If the target takes Fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute), the target takes an extra [[/damage 5 type=fire]] damage from burning oil.

Dousing a Space. You can take the Utilize action to pour an Oil flask on level ground to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself. If lit, the oil burns until the end of the turn 2 rounds from when the oil was lit (or 12 seconds) and deals 5 Fire damage to any creature that enters the area or ends its turn there. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

Fuel. Oil serves as fuel for Lamps and Lanterns. Once lit, a flask of Oil burns for 6 hours in a Lamp or Lantern. That duration doesn’t need to be consecutive; you can extinguish the burning Oil (as a Utilize action) and rekindle it again until it has burned for a total of 6 hours.
Rations consist of travel-ready food, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts. See &Reference[Malnutrition] in the rules glossary for the risks of not eating.

As a Utilize action, you can tie a knot with Rope if you succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. The Rope can be burst with a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check.

You can bind an unwilling creature with the Rope only if the creature has the &Reference[Grappled], &Reference[Incapacitated], or &Reference[Restrained] condition. If the creature’s legs are bound, the creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes. Escaping the Rope requires the creature to make a successful DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check as an action.

A Tinderbox is a small container holding flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a Candle, Lamp, Lantern, or Torch—or anything else with exposed fuel—takes a Bonus Action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.

A pale moonstone on a fine silver chain — a family heirloom from Chondalwood, and the one piece of home Jetten carries. He keeps it close to his heart; it reminds him of his people and especially his sister. By moonlight the stone holds a faint, milky glow, and Jetten — a devotee of Sehanine Moonbow — takes that as her quiet attention.

Sentimental value only; it has no magic the party has found. Losing it would wound Jetten more than any blade.

A rain-swollen sketchbook of hand-drawn trail maps — game paths, fords, safe springs, and campsites, marked in a guide's shorthand of dots and crescent moons. The earliest pages, in a younger hand, trace Chondalwood; then Arrabar, the Dalelands, and nine years of the Sword Coast, the High Forest, and the Forlorn Hills. Several pages near the back are blank, waiting for country he hasn't walked yet.

A tiny carved whistle on a leather cord, no longer than a finger. Blown softly, it imitates a wood wren's call closely enough to fool anyone but another wren. He and a light-footed halfling companion once crossed half the Dalelands speaking only in birdcalls; that friend went down another road years ago, but Jetten still signals camp the same way — habit, or remembrance.

@UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbutlMagicalBer]{Ten berries} appear in your hand and are infused with magic for the duration. A creature can take a Bonus Action to eat one berry. Eating a berry restores 1 Hit Point, and the berry provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day.

Uneaten berries disappear when the spell ends.

Wondrous Item, Uncommon

Traded off a caravan guard on the Trade Way who was retiring to keep bees. It has carried more arrows than any quiver its size has a right to, and still smells of oiled leather and long roads.

Each of the quiver’s three compartments connects to an extradimensional space that allows the quiver to hold numerous items while never weighing more than 2 pounds. The shortest compartment can hold up to 60 Arrows, Bolts, or similar objects. The midsize compartment holds up to 18 Javelins or similar objects. The longest compartment holds up to 6 long objects, such as bows, Quarterstaffs, or Spears.

You can draw any item the quiver contains as if doing so from a regular quiver or scabbard.

Weapon (Dagger), Uncommon

Dredged from the Delimbiyr in a fisherman's net, bright as the day it was lost. The river kept it sharp; nobody knows for whom.

You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

A small wooden disc, sanded smooth and stamped with a sheaf of grain — the mark of Chauntea, the Great Mother. Brother Tobin presses one on every traveller he blesses, “for a full belly and a soft road.” It is worth nothing and means a good deal.
A Healer’s Kit has ten uses. As a Utilize action, you can expend one of its uses to stabilize an Unconscious creature that has 0 Hit Points without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

A slender, fey-forged scimitar, its curve chased with gold that catches a light not quite there. It was the blade of a duelist of the fey roads, said never to have cut an innocent — lost with its bearer to the webs of a hidden temple in the Misty Forest, and dormant ever since, its old dawn waiting on a worthy hand.

To such a hand its fey magic stirs: once between dawns it throws off a bloom of clinging faerie light that lets nothing hide in shadow.

unidentified.description:
A slender scimitar, its curved blade chased with fine gold and its grip bound in worn green leather — the steel seems to catch a faint light that isn't quite there.

The blade keeps its own history close. Only one who attunes to it will learn what it truly is, and all that it has witnessed.
